summary: The note-candidates Dreamer pass can now take several model samples per fire and union them, and asks the model for a verdict on every message in the batch before it proposes any notebook entry. Six scenarios were added to its eval corpus, including an adversarial negative and a Cantonese-only twin.
details: Why: measured 2026-09-08 across four prompt variants, one shape of entry — a plan ONE person states with an unsettled corner, nobody having replied — is recognised in about 30% of samples, while precision stayed 1.00 on every negative sample of every variant. Three instruction-level changes (an explicit rule, a rewritten doctrine, a worked example) and two runtime ones (reasoning low, rendering the local weekday) did not move it. Two external reviews, given only the scenarios and the numbers, independently named the same two levers: an intermediate per-message representation, and sampling the temperature already being paid for.

`AdaptorSchedule.samples` (default 1) is model calls per fire; `DreamerRuntime.run` unions the readable ones, collapsing byte-identical items, and is `unavailable` only when NO sample was readable — one unreadable sample is counted on the new `nora_dream_sample_total{adaptor,status}` and skipped, so a batch that was read does not hold its watermark. A blank `inputs` still takes no sample at all.

`[notes] candidate_samples` (default 1, max 10) sets it for `note-candidates`. At the measured per-sample rate the union recognises the missed shape with probability 1 - 0.7^N: 0.66 at three samples, 0.83 at five. Cost is N calls on a pass that fires at most hourly per room and only when the room spoke.

`note-candidates.md` is version 5. The envelope carries `verdicts` — one entry per message, in order — before `candidates`, so each message is read on its own rather than the batch judged as a whole. Each verdict says three things: is something ahead, has somebody actually COMMITTED to it, and which corners are open. A NEW entry may only come from a message that is committed AND has an open corner; updating something the notebook already tracks is the explicit exception and needs no open corner.

Version 4 shipped only `ahead` and was measured a regression: it fixed the target case (3/10 -> 9/10) and cost the precision that had been 1.00 — «we should do a trip sometime» became a note in 8 of 10 samples, and the update path collapsed (10/10 -> 4/10) because a message that SETTLES something has no open corner. Under three unioned samples precision fell to 0.63 and a plan cancelled in its own batch became a note. v5 adds the `committed` half and the update exception, which is what the external review had actually specified.

`note-candidates`' `batch_limit` drops from 200 to 80, and that is a CONSEQUENCE of the verdict shape rather than a cost preference: the output now scales with the batch, and an output cap that binds truncates the JSON, which reads as `unavailable`, which HOLDS the watermark — so an over-long batch would be re-read and re-truncated on every fire, forever. A room that says more than 80 things in an hour drains over the following fires.

The eval corpus grows from ten cases to sixteen: a solo update to an existing entry, a Cantonese-only twin of the one-person plan, a plan stated and cancelled in the same batch (every surface feature of a positive), an invitation nobody picks up, a settled solo plan with nothing open, and a conditional.

Measured on the deployed model at reasoning none, 16 cases x 10 samples: v2 (before) precision 1.00 / recall 0.82 over the ten cases that existed; v4 0.77 / 0.76; v5 1.00 / 0.84 with all sixteen cases majority-passing and all ninety negative samples clean. The target case — a plan one person states with an unsettled corner — went 3/10 -> 10/10.

Sampling measured on top of v5, three unioned samples, 16 cases x 5: recall 1.00 (every positive case correct in every sample) and precision 0.95 — one negative, a settled solo plan, leaked in 2 of 5. That is the trade the union makes and it is why the knob ships at 1: raising it buys the last of the recall and spends a little of the precision, and which of those a notebook wants is the operator's call, not a default.
limitations: `candidate_samples` ships at 1, so nothing changes for a deployment until an operator raises it. The union's arithmetic assumes samples are roughly independent, and it only stays safe while per-sample invention is near zero — which v4 measured is what happens when it is not.

The 80-message batch cap is a bound, not a measurement: no eval case is long enough to exercise it, and the reading that would reopen it is a per-adaptor `[dreamer.budgets.note-candidates] output_tokens` sized for a longer batch.

The verdict shape is graded only through its effect on the notebook. Nothing asserts that the verdicts themselves are correct, and a model could produce good verdicts and a bad entry list — which is exactly the diagnostic split it was added to expose, read from the trace by eye.
